new.title: Climb up to Burg Altena above the Lenne valley
new.desc: Burg Altena stands on a rock spur above the Lenne and is traditionally dated to about 1108. In 1914 teacher Richard Schirrmann founded the world's first permanent youth hostel in the castle, and the museums cover the County of Mark, blacksmithing and hiking.
new.tip: Take the Erlebnisaufzug, a 60 m lift through the rock that opened in 2014, from the foot of the Klusenberg up to the courtyard.

new.title: Walk through the Dechenhöhle stalactite cave
new.desc: Dechenhöhle in Iserlohn-Letmathe was discovered by two railway workers on 10 June 1868 and has been open to visitors since. The cave is 902 m long, of which about 400 m is lit for the guided tour.
new.tip: The tour takes about 40 minutes. The German Cave Museum next door shows cave bear and woolly rhinoceros finds, and the Letmathe-Dechenhöhle rail stop is beside the entrance.

new.title: Explore the Henrichshütte blast furnace in Hattingen
new.desc: The Henrichshütte was founded in 1854, and blast furnace 3 dates from 1939-40. The last tapping was on 18 December 1987, and the site is now the LWL Industrial Museum and a stop on the Route of Industrial Culture.
new.tip: Concerts take place in the Gebläsehalle (blower hall), and the on-site restaurant is open Tuesday to Sunday daytime.

new.title: See the 1899 ship lift at Henrichenburg
new.desc: The old Schiffshebewerk Henrichenburg in Waltrop was built 1894-1899 and went into service on 11 August 1899 on the Dortmund-Ems Canal. It was taken out of service in 1969 and is now part of the LWL Industrial Museum in the Schleusenpark.
new.tip: Museum ships lie in the upper water, and the lock park is pleasant for a walk along the canal.

new.title: Go up the Glass Elephant in Maximilianpark Hamm
new.desc: The Glaselefant is a walk-in sculpture about 40 m high by artist Horst Rellecke, with a viewing platform at 35 m. It was built for the 1984 North Rhine-Westphalia garden show on the grounds of the former Maximilian colliery.
new.tip: The park also holds a tropical butterfly house, a museum railway and a lake. Dogs are not allowed except guide dogs.

new.title: Visit the Sri Kamadchi Ampal Hindu temple in Hamm
new.desc: This Tamil Hindu temple in Hamm-Uentrop was inaugurated on 7 July 2002 and is one of the largest in Europe. The hall temple is 27 by 27 m, and the entrance tower is 17 m high.
new.tip: Remove shoes before entering, no meat or alcohol on the grounds, and no photography during pujas. The sanctuary itself is closed to visitors.
new.q: Sri Kamadchi Ampal Tempel, Siegenbeckstraße, Hamm-Uentrop

new.title: Discover Zeche Nachtigall at the Muttental gateway
new.desc: Zeche Nachtigall in Witten-Bommern closed as a mine in 1892, and a brickworks followed until 1964. The LWL museum opened in 2003 and shows the way into the pit, a ring kiln and the brickworks chimney.
new.tip: The museum is seasonal, with a café and beer garden on site. Check the LWL site for the current dates.

new.title: Visit Schloss Cappenberg and its Stein park
new.desc: Count Gottfried founded the first Premonstratensian house in German-speaking lands here in 1122. After 1803 the abbey became a palace, and statesman Freiherr vom Stein lived here from 1817 to 1831. It now houses a museum, and the church St. Johannes Evangelist dates back to 1122.
new.tip: The 1899 water tower in the park serves as a lookout. A winery tavern by the Graf von Kanitz estate operates on site.

new.title: Stand in the giant portal of the Balver Höhle
new.desc: The Balver Höhle in the Hönne valley has an 11 m high, 18 m wide portal and is among the largest cave halls in Germany. Over 40,000 Middle Palaeolithic artefacts were found here, and since 1922 concerts, plays and the local Schützenfest have been held inside.
new.tip: Outside events the cave is open only to pre-registered groups, so check the festival calendar for the Balver Märchenwochen.

new.title: Explore the Burg Hardenstein ruin above the Ruhr
new.desc: The moated castle was built about 1345-1354 for the Hardenberg family, and the ruin lies in Witten-Herbede in a nature reserve. Restoration was completed in 2012 after a wall collapse in 2010.
new.tip: The Muttental mining trail starts behind the south wall, and a small ferry crosses the Ruhr nearby.

new.title: Tour Schloss Hohenlimburg above the Lenne
new.desc: Count Dietrich I of Altena-Isenberg had the castle built shortly before 1242, and it was the seat of the County of Limburg until 1807. Today it holds a small museum, a baroque garden and the mummified Schwarze Hand in the keep.
new.tip: Admission covers the courtyard, wall walk and keep. See schloss-hohenlimburg.de for opening hours.

new.title: Climb the keep of Burg Blankenstein in Hattingen
new.desc: Count Adolf I von der Mark founded this castle in 1226 on a rock ridge about 70 m above the Ruhr. The square tower is about 26 m high and has been open to visitors since 1971, and a restaurant occupies the neighbouring building.
new.tip: The castle restaurant and beer garden sit in the courtyard. Opening of the tower may be seasonal, so check ahead.

new.title: See abstract art at the Emil Schumacher Museum
new.desc: Opened on 28 August 2009 in Hagen's Kunstquartier, the museum holds about 500 works by Hagen-born painter Emil Schumacher from 1936 to 1999. The exposed-concrete building sits within a glass shell next to the Osthaus Museum.
new.tip: Temporary exhibitions change several times a year, so check the programme on the museum website.

new.title: Visit the moated Haus Martfeld in Schwelm
new.desc: Haus Martfeld grew from a 14th-century moated castle, with a round tower of about 1450 and a baroque form from 1752. It houses the Schwelm local history museum, the city archive and a neo-Gothic burial chapel in the park.
new.tip: The park is a quiet stop, and the museum covers the Schwelm limestone reef fossils.

new.title: Meet the Romans at the LWL Roman Museum in Haltern
new.desc: The museum shows finds from the Roman camps on the Lippe, which excavators first sought at the Annaberg in 1899. Visitors see legionary life, crafts and about 15,000 Playmobil figures, and a reconstructed camp gate (Römerbaustelle Aliso) opened beside it in 2016.
new.tip: Combine with a walk to the Aliso reconstruction next door.
new.q: LWL-Römermuseum, Weseler Straße 100, Haltern am See

new.title: See the world's only light-art museum in Unna
new.desc: The Zentrum für Internationale Lichtkunst has occupied the cold cellars of the former Lindenbrauerei since 2001. Works by artists such as James Turrell, Olafur Eliasson and Rebecca Horn are shown, and Mario Merz's Fibonacci numbers glow on the brewery chimney.
new.tip: The brewery complex also has a venue, an in-house brewery and a cultural programme at Rio-Reiser-Weg 1.
new.q: Zentrum für Internationale Lichtkunst, Lindenplatz 1, Unna

new.title: Learn Jewish history at the Jewish Museum in Dorsten
new.desc: The Jüdisches Museum Westfalen opened on 28 June 1992 and was redesigned in 2001 and 2018. Its permanent exhibition L'Chaim! covers Jewish religion, customs and Westphalian life through 16 biographies.
new.tip: A sculpture garden lies behind the building, and temporary exhibitions rotate.

new.title: Stroll around the moated Schloss Herten and its park
new.desc: Schloss Herten is a baroque moated castle rebuilt by 1702 after a fire in 1687, with an outer ward on its own island. The 30-hectare park was reshaped in 1814-17 by Maximilian Friedrich Weyhe as an English landscape garden.
new.tip: The park is open to the public. The castle itself hosts concerts such as the Klavier-Festival Ruhr.

new.title: Visit Schloss Wittringen and its bird island in Gladbeck
new.desc: This moated castle goes back to a 1263 charter and was rebuilt around 1650 after Hessian troops destroyed it in 1642. The city bought it in 1922, and a half-timbered house holds the Gladbeck museum.
new.tip: The surrounding Wittringen leisure park includes the Vogelinsel with parrots and exotic birds.

new.title: Wander the half-timbered old town of Hattingen
new.desc: Hattingen's Altstadt around the Untermarkt and Obermarkt has a dense ring of half-timbered houses above the Ruhr. It is a short walk from the Henrichshütte and Burg Blankenstein.
new.tip: The cafés and restaurants around Untermarkt make a good stop after the sights.

new.title: Eat at the Danzturm tower restaurant above Iserlohn
new.desc: The 28 m Danzturm opened on 22 May 1909 on the Telegraphenberg at 384.5 m and is named after Professor Ernst Danz. The view covers the Sauerland and the Hellweg as far as Dortmund, Unna and Hamm, and a panorama restaurant sits at its foot.
new.tip: Tower admission is free while the restaurant is open, which is daily from 11:00 according to listings.

new.title: Refuel at Forsthaus Löhen after a Iserlohn forest walk
new.desc: Forsthaus Löhen is a rustic forest inn on Löhenweg in Iserlohn that serves German and regional dishes. It is a popular stop for hikers, and mains cost roughly 10 to 20 euros per listings.
new.tip: Opening hours vary by listing, so check before setting out. Outdoor seating is available.

new.title: Eat smoked trout at the Brenscheider Mühle
new.desc: The Waldrestaurant Brenscheider Mühle in the Nahmerbach valley near Nachrodt-Wiblingwerde is known for smoked trout from its own ponds. A grain mill stands beside it and an oil mill of 1845 nearby.
new.tip: There is a beer garden in good weather. Hours listed are limited, so call ahead.
new.q: Waldrestaurant Brenscheider Mühle, Brenscheider Mühle 1, Nachrodt-Wiblingwerde

new.title: Have lunch at Henrichs beside the Henrichshütte
new.desc: Henrichs is the restaurant on the Henrichshütte site, serving fresh and Mediterranean cooking in an industrial-heritage setting. It is run by Henrichs Eventgastronomie and linked to concerts in the blower hall.
new.tip: Open Tuesday to Sunday 12:00-18:00 per its website, with other times by request.

new.title: Dine in the water castle Haus Kemnade in Hattingen
new.desc: The Burgstuben at Haus Kemnade sit in a water castle dating from the 13th century in the Ruhr valley. The kitchen is traditional German, with game schnitzel, baked salmon and grilled rump steak recommended.
new.tip: Mains cost about 20 to 36 euros. It opens Wednesday to Sunday, with 100 outdoor seats.
new.q: Haus Kemnade Burgstuben, An der Kemnade 10, Hattingen

new.title: Try Westphalian cooking at Fachwerk in Hattingen
new.desc: Fachwerk on the Untermarkt cooks Westphalian dishes with Mediterranean and Eastern touches, such as duck leg with carrot puree or cheek with black pudding. It holds a Michelin Plate.
new.tip: Goose menus appear in the cooler months. Book for evenings.

new.title: Order cake at Café Adele in Hattingen's old town
new.desc: Café Adele is a small café in the historic Altstadt of Hattingen, praised for its cakes, coffee and service. It averages 4.5 out of 5 on speisekarte.menu.
new.tip: Combine with a walk through the half-timbered lanes. Opening hours vary, so check before visiting.

new.title: Eat Sauerbraten and kale at Haus Splietker in Hamm
new.desc: Haus Splietker in Süddinker serves Westphalian home cooking, known for Sauerbraten and Rouladen. Seasonal dishes include Grünkohl with Kasseler and Kohlwurst, and game and goose roasts.
new.tip: Open Wednesday to Saturday evenings and Sunday from noon, with two beer gardens.

new.title: Drink house-brewed beer at Suberg's bei Boente
new.desc: Suberg's bei Boente - Die Hausbrauerei is a brewery with restaurant on Augustinessenstraße in Recklinghausen's old town. It scores 4.7 on OpenTable from 228 reviews.
new.tip: It also offers a historic pub-history city tour. Book a table at weekends.
new.q: Suberg's bei Boente - die Hausbrauerei, Augustinessenstraße 4, Recklinghausen

new.title: Stop for a beer garden meal at the Rohrmeisterei Schwerte
new.desc: The Rohrmeisterei at Ruhrstraße 20 is a converted industrial hall on the Ruhr with the Bistro Unter'm Kran, the Restaurant Glaskasten and a large beer garden. The gastronomy opened in 2003.
new.tip: It is a stop on the Ruhrtalradweg, with a bike service station out front.

new.title: Drink LindenBier from the in-house brewery in Unna
new.desc: The Kultur- und Kommunikationszentrum Lindenbrauerei advertises LindenBier fresh from its in-house brewery. Linden Pils is again brewed in showcase copper kettles in the old brewery, which closed in 1979.
new.tip: Check the programme at lindenbrauerei.de for events and opening times.

new.title: Cycle the Hengsteysee loop between Hagen and Herdecke
new.desc: A path of about 6.5 km circles the Hengsteysee, built 1927-1929, and its south side is part of the Ruhrtalradweg. Sailing, rowing and canoe clubs line the shore, and Hohensyburg stands above its start.
new.tip: In warm months the passenger ship Freiherr vom Stein runs between the Herdecke landing and the Lenne mouth.

new.title: Walk the Muttental mining trail past Burg Hardenstein
new.desc: The Muttental valley in Witten holds the Bergbauwanderweg through the early hard coal mining area. The trail starts directly behind the south wall of Burg Hardenstein and links to Zeche Nachtigall.
new.tip: A small Ruhr ferry, Hardenstein, runs near the ruin. Wear sturdy shoes.

new.title: Walk the 8 km path around the Haltern reservoir
new.desc: The Halterner Stausee covers 307 ha and supplies drinking water for over a million people. An 8.3 km circuit path runs around it, and the ship Möwe sails on the lake.
new.tip: The Seebad Haltern beach has an 800 m sandy shore for swimming. Motorboats are generally not allowed.
new.q: Halterner Stausee, Stockwieser Damm, Haltern am See

new.title: Go caving in the Kluterthöhle in Ennepetal
new.desc: The Kluterthöhle has about 8.7 km of surveyed passages, of which 1,080 m is a show cave. Besides regular tours it offers adventure tours through narrow passages with a torch and sturdy footwear.
new.tip: Book adventure tours in advance, and bring warm clothes.

new.title: See a play at the Ruhrfestspiele in Recklinghausen
new.desc: The Ruhrfestspiele began in 1947 from the Kohle gegen Kunst exchange between miners and Hamburg theatres. The season runs roughly from 1 May to mid-June in the festival house on the hill.
new.tip: Book tickets early for headline productions.

new.title: Hike up Halde Hoheward to the sundial
new.desc: Halde Hoheward between Herten and Recklinghausen reaches 152.5 m. On its southern plateau stands a stainless steel obelisk 8.5 m high that works as a sundial.
new.tip: The Horizont-Observatorium opened in 2008 but was closed after cracks appeared, so check access.

new.title: Ride the Erlebnisaufzug up to Burg Altena
new.desc: The lift opened on 26 April 2014 and runs 60 m vertically through the rock from the foot of the Klusenberg to the castle courtyard. It is a paid ride that saves the climb.
new.tip: Combine with a visit to the castle museums above.

new.title: Watch craftspeople at work in the Hagen open-air museum
new.desc: The LWL open-air museum in Mäckingerbach opened to the public in 1973 and has about 60 reconstructed workshops across 42 hectares. A working brewery, a bakery, the German Blacksmithing Museum and a relocated windmill are among the stations.
new.tip: Open 1 April to 31 October, with a Christmas market on the first Advent weekend. The brewery has been run by Braumanufaktur Pohlmann since 2019.

new.title: Join the chariot festival at the Hamm Hindu temple
new.desc: The annual 14-day chariot festival at the Sri Kamadchi Ampal temple in Hamm-Uentrop takes place in May or June. It draws over 15,000 worshippers and visitors.
new.tip: Respect temple rules, which include no shoes, no meat and no photography during pujas.
